text:
sam: Hey team — I accepted the org invite earlier but when I try to open a PR against redwood/core-sdk I get a 404 on the repo page in the browser and `remote: Repository not found.` from git. I can see other public repos fine. Who should I bug?

emily: Welcome! Quick Q: are you signed in to the same GitHub account we invited? Some folks have personal account vs work account confusion.

sam: I think so. My profile shows my work email but my GitHub username is 'sammyp'. The invite email was my work address.

terra: If you accepted under a different GH account that can cause a 404. Go to https://github.com/orgs/redwood/people and search for your username. If you don't show up, the invite probably landed on another account.

sam: I'm not listed in the org people page. But the invite link said accepted.

emily: Two possibilities: 1) the invite was accepted by a different GitHub account that uses the same email alias, 2) SSO/org provisioning needs a sync. Can you paste the invite email you accepted (screenshot ok) and your GitHub account link?

sam: Sent screenshot in DM — it's the invite to sam@redwood.com and I clicked Accept. My profile: https://github.com/sammyp

terra: Thanks. @people-ops can you check if sam@redwood.com is associated with the sammyp account or if there's a separate account that accepted?

people-ops: Looking now. We see an account 'sam-corp' that accepted the invite using sam@redwood.com as a secondary email. That means the org membership is tied to sam-corp, not sammyp. If you want membership on sammyp instead, we need the sammyp account to add sam@redwood.com as a verified email and then re-invite, or we can transfer the membership to the sammyp handle. Which do you prefer?

sam: sammyp is my main public handle. I can add the work email to it. How do I verify?

emily: In GitHub: Settings -> Emails -> Add email -> verify using the confirmation email. After that we can remove the invite from sam-corp and re-invite sammyp (or people-ops can transfer). Also if your sammyp account has 2FA off, org will block access until 2FA is enabled.

sam: I added sam@redwood.com to sammyp and verified it. I also turned on 2FA.

people-ops: Great. I removed the old acceptance from sam-corp and sent a fresh invite to sammyp. Accept that and then check `gh repo view redwood/core-sdk --json viewerPermission` or try cloning.

sam: Accepted. Cloning works now and I can push to my branch. Still getting a permissions error when I try to push to the main branch — I think that's expected.

terra: Correct — main is protected. Create a branch and open a PR. If you need write to a specific auxiliary repo, tell us which and we'll confirm team membership.

sam: One small ask: could people-ops annotate the onboarding doc with the email->account gotcha? Took me a bit to realize which account accepted.

emily: Good call. Adding a short note and a checklist:
- Confirm invited email is present on the intended GitHub account (Settings -> Emails)
- Verify email and enable 2FA before accepting org invite
- If the wrong account accepted, people-ops can revoke and re-invite
- For CLI auth, run `gh auth status` and `gh auth login` after accepting to refresh tokens

sam: Thanks everyone, sorry for the noise. All set now :smile:
